OpenAI models

OpenAI was announced in December 2015 as a non-profit artificial intelligence research company and states its mission as ensuring that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. It develops the GPT language models, the o-series reasoning models and the open-weight gpt-oss models, and offers its models through ChatGPT and the OpenAI API.

Google models

Google, headquartered in Mountain View, California, makes hundreds of products, among them Google Search, YouTube, Android and Gmail. Its AI research unit, Google DeepMind, was formed in 2023 by combining Google Brain and DeepMind. Google's language models include LaMDA, PaLM and the Gemini line, and since 2024 it has also released open-weights models under the Gemma name.

Claude Fable 5.2

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Fable 5.2 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Fable line and the successor to Claude Fable 5.1, released on 9 November 2026. Anthropic describes it as the same underlying model as Claude Mythos 5.2, with cybersecurity and biology safeguards that allow general availability, and lists token prices of 8 USD per million input tokens and 40 USD per million output tokens. Gemini 4 Argon

PreviewLanguage, Multimodal, ReasoningMilestone

Gemini 4 Argon is a reasoning model in Google's Gemini line, announced on 30 September 2026 and first rolled out only to vetted cyber defenders in the Fairwind Program. Google describes it as built for sustained reasoning over long, multi-step work in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and cybersecurity defense, with output of up to 1M tokens. [1][2]

GPT-6.1 Sol

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

GPT-6.1 Sol is the first model of OpenAI's GPT-6.1 family, a reasoning language model for text and image input released on 29 September 2026 in the API and in ChatGPT Work and Codex for paid and Edu plans. OpenAI presents it as an upgrade to GPT-6 Sol at a fifth of GPT-6 Astra's standard token prices, and rates it Critical in cybersecurity. [1][2][3][4][5]

Claude Sonnet 5.5

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Sonnet line, released on 28 September 2026 on all platforms at the same price as Claude Sonnet 5; Anthropic calls it the second model of its Claude 5.5 family. Anthropic says it is the first Sonnet model with classifiers that block reasoning extraction, and its thinking blocks are tied to the account that produced them. [1][2]September 28, 2026

Claude Opus 5.5

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Opus 5.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line and, according to Anthropic, the first model of its Claude 5.5 family, released on 22 September 2026 on all platforms. It costs less per token than Claude Opus 5, has adaptive thinking that cannot be switched off, is available with zero data retention and carries Anthropic's output watermarking. GPT-6 Luna

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

GPT-6 Luna is the Luna tier of OpenAI's GPT-6 family, a reasoning language model for text and image input that the API docs describe as meant for focused, high-volume tasks. It was released with GPT-6 Sol on 22 September 2026 in the API, Amazon Bedrock, ChatGPT Work and Codex, where Free and Go users can use it in the desktop app, but not in ChatGPT conversations. GPT-6 Sol

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

GPT-6 Sol is the Sol tier of OpenAI's GPT-6 family, a reasoning language model for text and image input that OpenAI describes as a lower-cost alternative to GPT-6 Astra, trained with similar methods. It was released with GPT-6 Luna on 22 September 2026 in the API, Amazon Bedrock, ChatGPT Work and Codex, but not in ChatGPT conversations. [1][2][3][4][5]

Grok 4.7

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Grok 4.7 is a language model in xAI's Grok line for text and image input, released on 21 September 2026 on the xAI API, in Cursor and in Grok Build, where it is the default model, and through third-party tools and cloud platforms. xAI says it uses a new, larger base model than Grok 4.6 and a longer reinforcement learning run aimed at tasks that take many hours. [1][2][3]

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 552B backbone parameters that takes text and images and generates text, released on 2026-09-10 in the DeepSeek API as deepseek-flash and with open weights under the MIT License. DeepSeek calls it the smallest model of a new architecture family and says it was trained from scratch. [1]Introduction; License[2]

GPT-6 Astra

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, ReasoningMilestone

GPT-6 Astra is the first model of OpenAI's GPT-6 generation, a reasoning language model for text and image input released on 3 September 2026 in ChatGPT Work, Codex, the API and Amazon Bedrock, after a first rollout to a limited set of organizations. OpenAI says it is its first model to reach the Critical level of cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework. [1][2][3][4][5]

Gemini 3.8 Flash

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Gemini 3.8 Flash is a multimodal reasoning model in Google's Flash line with adjustable effort levels, released on 2 September 2026 and based on Gemini 3.7 Flash. Google aims it at long-horizon software engineering, autonomous agents and enterprise workflows; it was offered through the Gemini API, Google Antigravity, Stitch and Gemini Enterprise, and to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. [1][2][3]September 2, 2026

Muse Spark 1.3

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Muse Spark 1.3 is a multimodal reasoning model in Meta's Muse series, offered in the Meta Model API and the Muse Code terminal agent. Meta says it improves agentic and coding work and is easier to use; it adds a max reasoning effort level on the Standard tier, and the API docs say its audio understanding is not fully supported. Claude Fable 5.1

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Fable 5.1 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Fable line and the successor to Claude Fable 5, released on 1 September 2026 on the Claude apps, the Claude API and major cloud platforms. Anthropic says it is the same model as Claude Mythos 5.1 with different safeguards; token prices match Fable 5, cache reads cost less, and its text carries Anthropic's watermark. Claude Opus 4.5

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Opus 4.5 is a language model in Anthropic's Opus line that accepts text and images, with a 200K-token context window, extended thinking and an effort parameter for trading thoroughness against token use. It is offered in the Claude apps, on the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry, at a lower price than earlier Opus models. [1]Capabilities[2][3]Claude Opus 4.5 Summary Table, Access Surfaces[4]November 24, 2025

Claude Opus 4.6

AvailableLanguage, Multimodal, Reasoning

Claude Opus 4.6 is a language model in Anthropic's Claude Opus line, released on 5 February 2026 on claude.ai, the Claude API and major cloud platforms. It takes text and image input, launched with adaptive thinking and with context compaction in beta, and has a 1M token context window that was in beta at launch. [1][2]Capabilities

About AI Radar

A personal, non-commercial project by Benjamin Nieuwenhuijzen.

On this page

  1. What the dashboard shows
  2. Where the posts come from
  3. Model History
  4. What is automated, and therefore fallible
  5. Who makes it

AI Radar is a live dashboard that collects the latest news and updates from the leading AI companies on one page. Every post links straight to the original article. Next to the news, Model History records which AI models those companies released, when, and what changed, with the sources behind every fact.

What the dashboard shows

At the top, the Today in AI carousel shows a handful of top stories, picked automatically from the latest posts and labelled Auto-selected. Next to it, the Latest column lists the five newest posts. A live status line shows when the data was last updated, counts down to the next scheduled refresh and gives the number of sources.

Each company has its own card, from OpenAI and Anthropic to Mistral, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI (Kimi). The Across AI card adds industry news that is not tied to a single company. You can switch between two views, By company and Timeline, narrow the posts down with the category chips or search, and save posts for later. The Motion toggle turns off all movement on the page; this also happens automatically when your system asks for reduced motion.

Where the posts come from

AI Radar reads publicly available RSS and Atom feeds. Each card states its source: an official feed is maintained by the company itself, a community feed is maintained by others and may lag behind. A scheduled job fetches all feeds every two hours and rebuilds the page data. Nothing is rewritten or shortened by hand; posts appear as their source published them.

Model History

Model History is AI Radar's own content: a history of the models of the same companies, with a page per company, a page and a timeline per model, and the relations between models (which one succeeded, revised or was derived from which). Dates are shown exactly as precisely as the sources give them: if a source names only the month, the page shows only the month. Every fact links to its sources, and each source shows whether the original is still online or only available as an archived copy.

The records are compiled from the organisations' own announcements, model cards and documentation. The summaries and change notes are drafted with the help of an AI assistant from those sources and checked against them. Newly released models are added by an AI agent (see below). It is not a benchmark or a ranking: there are no scores, and claims made by a company are attributed to it.

What is automated, and therefore fallible

Several things on the site are produced by software rather than a person, and each one can be wrong:

  • Categories (Model releases, Products, Research and so on) are assigned from a post's title and summary. A mislabelled post is an estimate gone wrong, not an editorial judgement.
  • Card order follows recent news activity.
  • The "Today in AI" stories at the top are picked by a simple rule: recent model releases first, at most one per company. No AI model writes or rewrites them; each slide shows the post's own title and summary.
  • Source status in Model History ("Active", "Archived copy", "Unavailable") comes partly from a daily automatic check of each source address, run on GitHub's servers. A site that blocks the check or is briefly down can be marked wrongly for a while.
  • Related AI Radar coverage on a model page is linked automatically when a post's title or summary contains one of the model's names. A link can be missing or, now and then, point to the wrong model.
  • New models in Model History: when AI Radar posts name a model that has no page yet, an AI agent looks up the organisation's own sources once a day, writes the record and its summary, and publishes it after automatic checks of the data. No person reads these entries before they appear, so a new entry can contain a mistake until it is corrected.

For anything that matters, click through and read the original article.

Who makes it

AI Radar is made and maintained by Benjamin Nieuwenhuijzen. It is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, any of the companies it follows. All rights to the posts remain with their original sources, as set out in the Disclaimer. The dashboard needs no account and collects no personal data about you; the details are in the Privacy Statement.

Suggestions for new sources, corrections and other feedback are welcome via the contact page. Prefer your own reader? There is an RSS feed with everything combined.

Contact

AI Radar is a personal, non-commercial project by Benjamin Nieuwenhuijzen.

On this page

  1. What you can write about
  2. Source and removal requests
  3. Privacy
  4. Elsewhere

Questions, feedback or a request about AI Radar? The fastest way to reach me is by email. I read everything and try to reply within a few days.

Emailinfo@ai-radar.eu

What you can write about

  • Feedback and suggestions: ideas for new companies or sources to follow, features, or anything that feels off.
  • Corrections: a post in the wrong category, a broken link, or a source that is out of date; in Model History also a wrong date, name or relation, a source marked with the wrong status, or a news post linked to the wrong model.
  • Removal requests: see the note below if you are a rights holder.
  • Press and partnerships: collaborations, listings or anything commercial.

Source and removal requests

The dashboard reads publicly available feeds and links each item back to the original article. All rights to the posts remain with their original sources, as set out in the Disclaimer. If you are a rights holder and would like a reference to your content removed, email info@ai-radar.eu with the link in question and I will act on reasonable requests promptly.

Model History is a historical record, so a justified request there removes the link to your page, while the factual entry (the model, its date and the name of the source) stays, marked as not linked at the rights holder's request.

Privacy

Emailing me means I receive your email address and your message, used only to reply to you. AI Radar has no contact form and stores nothing on its side. How the dashboard itself handles data is described in the Privacy Statement.

Elsewhere

You can also find me on LinkedIn, X, Instagram and GitHub.

Privacy Statement

Last updated: 1 October 2026

On this page

  1. 1. Who is responsible
  2. 2. What is stored on your device
  3. 3. Hosting and server logs
  4. 4. Where the content comes from
  5. 5. Email subscription (optional)
  6. 6. No personal data collected by AI Radar
  7. 7. Your rights
  8. 8. Audience
  9. 9. Changes to this statement

The short version. AI Radar is a free, personal, non-commercial dashboard that shows publicly available AI news, together with its Model History pages. There are no accounts, no advertising, no analytics and no tracking cookies. Everything runs in your own browser. Because the only data stored on your device is strictly functional, no cookie-consent banner is required.

1. Who is responsible

AI Radar is a personal project by Benjamin Nieuwenhuijzen. It is not a commercial service. For privacy questions you can reach the maintainer by email at info@ai-radar.eu or via the contact page.

2. What is stored on your device

AI Radar keeps a small amount of information in your browser's local storage so the dashboard remembers how you like to use it. This includes:

  • your theme preference (light or dark);
  • your motion preference (on or off);
  • the list of posts you saved.

This information stays on your device. It is never sent to AI Radar or to anyone else, and it is not used to identify or track you. Because it is strictly necessary for the functionality you requested, no consent is required for it under the GDPR and the ePrivacy rules. You can remove it at any time by clearing your browser's site data for this site. View and filter settings are not stored at all: they are kept in the page address (URL). What you type into a search box is never stored, put in the address or sent anywhere; it stays in the open page.

3. Hosting and server logs

The dashboard and its Model History pages are hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc.), which delivers them through its content delivery network (Fastly). As with any website, the host automatically receives standard technical request data, including your IP address, the type of browser you use and the page you requested, in order to deliver the page and keep the service secure. This processing is carried out by GitHub as the hosting provider. AI Radar has no analytics layer of its own and does not combine this data with anything else to identify you. GitHub's handling of this data is described in the GitHub Privacy Statement.

The domain name ai-radar.eu and the email address info@ai-radar.eu are provided by TransIP, which therefore processes the email you send to that address.

4. Where the content comes from

The posts and the model data you see are loaded from AI Radar's own pages and data files, served from the same domain. They are prepared in advance and contain no information about you, so viewing them involves no third party other than the host described above. Images are served from ai-radar.eu itself and the page loads no fonts from other services, so your browser makes no requests to third parties such as Google Fonts or image hosts.

When you open an article or a source, the link takes you to the original publisher's website or to an archived copy (for example at web.archive.org), which is outside AI Radar's control and has its own privacy policy. The automatic checks of source addresses run on GitHub's servers, never in your browser.

5. Email subscription (optional)

If you choose to subscribe to the AI Radar feed by email, this is handled by the third-party service Blogtrottr. You enter your email address at Blogtrottr and confirm it by email; your address never reaches AI Radar. The subscription is governed by Blogtrottr's privacy policy, and you can unsubscribe from any email.

6. No personal data collected by AI Radar

AI Radar itself has no accounts, no contact forms, no newsletter list and no profiling. It does not collect, sell or share personal data.

7. Your rights

Under the GDPR you have rights to access, correct and erase personal data, among others. Because AI Radar holds no personal data about you, there is nothing on its side to access or erase. For the data stored on your own device, you are in control: clear it through your browser at any time. For the technical request data handled by the host, see the GitHub Privacy Statement linked above. For any question, use the contact channel in section 1.

8. Audience

AI Radar is a general-interest news dashboard and is not directed at children.

9. Changes to this statement

This statement may be updated if the site changes. The date at the top shows when it was last revised.

In short. The dashboard is an aggregator, not a source: it reads publicly available feeds and shows them unchanged, with a link to each original article. Model History is AI Radar's own content, compiled from the companies' publications, with sources for every fact. No rights can be derived from what is shown, and AI Radar is not affiliated with any of the companies listed.

1. News: an aggregator, not a source

The news on the dashboard is not owned by AI Radar's creator. AI Radar only reads publicly available sources, the news feeds of the companies listed and community feeds, and displays them unchanged, each with a link to the original article. All rights to the posts remain with the original sources.

Model History is AI Radar's own editorial content: summaries, dates, relations between models and an assessment of each source, compiled from the organisations' own publications, with the summaries drafted with the help of an AI assistant; newly released models are added by an AI agent and published without prior human review. Claims made by a company are attributed to it; they are not AI Radar's endorsement of them.

2. No warranty and no rights

No rights can be derived from the information shown. The creator offers no guarantee as to the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of the data, and accepts no responsibility or liability for incorrect, outdated or incomplete posts, nor for any decisions made based on them. Community feeds in particular may lag behind the official source.

The same applies to Model History. Historical data can be incomplete or wrong, sources can disagree, and the status of a source (online, archived or unavailable) comes partly from an automatic check and can change. Where the evidence is incomplete, the page says so.

3. Automated categorisation

Each post is automatically assigned a category based on its title and summary. This is an automated estimate, not an editorial judgement, and it is not foolproof. Posts may occasionally be placed in a less fitting category.

4. Brand names and intellectual property

Brand names and logos mentioned are the property of their respective owners and are used here for identification purposes only. AI Radar is not affiliated with, sponsored by or endorsed by any of the companies listed.

5. External links

AI Radar links to external websites, including sources and archived copies such as those at web.archive.org. AI Radar has no control over those sites and is not responsible for their content, availability, terms or privacy practices. Visiting them is at your own discretion.

6. Email delivery

The optional email subscription is provided by the third-party service Blogtrottr. Your email address never reaches AI Radar, and the delivery of those emails falls outside the creator's responsibility.

7. A personal project

AI Radar is a personal, non-commercial project. How it handles your data is described in the Privacy Statement.

Start again from the dashboard for the latest AI news, or from Model History to look up a model. Renamed models keep a forwarding page, so an old model link usually still works; if this one should, please tell me via the contact page.
